methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prospective service evaluation in a real-world UK screening program, including 10,889 women whose mammograms were read during 27 February to 5 October 2023 with standard double reading preserved for all participants. The study evaluates live AI integration (AI-Additional Read workflow) plus simulations of 17 workflow variants, which allows direct estimation of detection/recall/workload tradeoffs under controlled assumptions. A key design strength is that routine readers and the primary arbitrator were blinded to AI output, and discordant AI-recall cases underwent additional senior arbitration with AI regions-of-interest, yielding 11 additional detected cancers. Limitations include single-region deployment, dependence on workflow simulation assumptions for many variants, and nonrandomized design, which can introduce operational and spectrum biases.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The evaluation follows a defined screening cohort prospectively within routine care and compares outcomes under different reading workflows, aligning most closely with an individual cohort study (Oxford LoE 2b) rather than an RCT. Clinical relevance is very high because it addresses population breast-cancer screening performance and workload constraints, reporting improvements such as a modeled 10.4% cancer-detection increase with maintained recall rate and up to ~31% workload reduction in the primary workflow. The design also tests operationally realistic integration points (live AI prompting additional review only when AI and double reading disagree), which maps directly to implementation decisions in screening services.

reporting_quality.justification: This is an AI-assisted diagnostic accuracy/workflow evaluation, making STARD the closest applicable reporting standard (and the manuscript cites STARD-AI in the references). Methods clearly describe the source population, dates, standard-of-care double reading and arbitration, AI operating points, and the live “AI-Additional Read” process, supporting interpretability of workflow comparisons. The reference list indicates public code availability (“Runnable GEMINI paper R code” deposited on Zenodo), which supports a strong reproducibility posture for the analytical workflow. Some STARD items such as full participant flow accounting and prespecified decision thresholds may be partially limited by the service-evaluation framing and normalization, but reporting appears broadly thorough.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is in a prospective, multi-workflow evaluation that combines live integration with simulation to compare 17 realistic AI deployment patterns rather than a single “AI vs humans” benchmark. The manuscript quantifies not only detection metrics but also operational impacts (workload reduction up to ~31–36%), which is a practical advance for screening-program decision-making. While AI in screening is an active area, the breadth of workflow permutations and the live-plus-simulated evaluation approach are meaningfully original.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract reports concrete cohort size (10,889), dates, and outcome deltas (for example 11 additional cancers and workload savings), making the claims easy to evaluate. Methods clearly separate routine care, live AI-assisted steps, and simulated workflow modeling, and define key outcomes (cancer detection, recall, PPV, sensitivity/specificity, workload). The manuscript is operationally dense but generally well structured and readable for a screening-audit style study.

key_strengths: Prospective real-world evaluation embedded in routine screening with standard double reading maintained for all participants.
Pragmatic workflow design: AI-triggered additional review only when AI recommends recall but routine decision does not, yielding additional detected cancers.
Comprehensive comparison across 17 workflow settings, including operational workload impacts alongside diagnostic metrics.
key_concerns: Nonrandomized, single-region service evaluation may limit generalizability and is vulnerable to operational/spectrum effects.
Many workflow comparisons rely on simulation assumptions that should be carefully justified and sensitivity-tested.
Full STARD-style flow accounting and prespecified threshold reporting may be incomplete in the normalized text.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Large, prospective, implementation-facing evidence on AI integration in screening with clear operational benefit; strong fit for a high-impact clinical/health-systems journal, with minor revisions focused on transparency around simulation assumptions and reporting completeness.
